point_one.new_listener_takeaway: The phrase “deploying weapons to space” should be reserved here for the newly acknowledged orbital deployment, whose system details remain undisclosed; Russia’s 2021 test, China’s 2007 test, and India’s 2019 test demonstrated weapons launched from Earth against satellites, not weapons permanently placed in orbit.
point_one.evidence_anchor: F-001 records the U.S. Air Force secretary’s statement that orbit-based space-control weapons had been deployed and the official description of it as the first such acknowledgment by the Space Force. F-003–F-005 document ground-launched ASAT tests, while F-002, F-009, and F-010 describe assessed or developing counterspace capabilities rather than confirmed orbital weapon deployments.
point_one.why_it_matters: This distinction tells listeners what is genuinely new in the current story instead of treating every past ASAT test as evidence that weapons have already been stationed in space. It also prevents undisclosed capabilities from being presented as known attack systems or assigned targets.

Use concrete cases to show that satellite disruption does not necessarily mean a satellite was physically attacked or destroyed.
